evals.name: bpmn-rental-booking-to-python
evals.prompt: Here's the BPMN export of our equipment rental process: evals/create-workflow-from-diagram/files/rental-booking.bpmn. Generate a Python Dapr workflow from it and call the project rentalBooking.
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the BPMN path and writes rentalBooking/.workflow.ir.jsonl using the single __type-keyed IR schema from prompts/ir-schema.md (metadata first, BPMN ids preserved, result + end_of_ir_stream last). Both end events are reachable (the waitlist decision leads to rentalDeclined). After validation it renders a Python project (three-way parallel preparation with when_all, human waitlist decision, bounded 2-day timer loop) with dapr.yaml, statestore, README and the exact final message, without installing or running anything. The input is deliberately different from the skill's own examples/order-process.bpmn so the run cannot copy the bundled example IR.
expectations: Creates rentalBooking/.workflow.ir.jsonl in which every non-empty line is a standalone JSON object with a `__type` field (no surrounding array, no markdown fences, no records keyed by a top-level `type` such as `workflow`, `start` or `end`)

The first IR record has `__type: "metadata"` with `source: "bpmn"` and `process_id: "rentalBooking"`; the last two records are `{"__type": "result", "success": true, ...}` followed by `{"__type": "end_of_ir_stream", ...}`

The IR keeps the BPMN element ids rentalRequested, verifyCustomer, checkAvailability, equipmentAvailable, prepareSplit, reserveEquipment, takeDeposit, sendContract, prepareJoin, offerWaitlist, joinsWaitlist, waitForReturns, rentalConfirmed and rentalDeclined, and contains no ids from the skill's bundled order-process example (such as checkInventory or waitForRestock)

In the IR, equipmentAvailable and joinsWaitlist are `__type: "gateway"` records with `type: "exclusive"` and `role: "diverging"` whose `flows` mark the BPMN default flow with `is_default: true`; prepareSplit is a `parallel` `diverging` gateway with three outgoing flows and prepareJoin a `parallel` `converging` gateway
In the IR, waitForReturns is an `activity` with `type: "wait_for_event"` whose `events` entry has `event_type: "timer"`, `event_definition: "P2D"` and `next: "checkAvailability"`

rentalRequested, rentalConfirmed and rentalDeclined are `__type: "start_end_node"` records (`type` start / end / end), and the IR contains an edge from joinsWaitlist to rentalDeclined so every end node is reachable

Creates rentalBooking/dapr.yaml and rentalBooking/resources/statestore.yaml with actorStateStore set to "true", plus Python files including workflow.py, activities.py, models.py, runtime.py, main.py and pyproject.toml
The generated workflow schedules the reserveEquipment, takeDeposit and sendContract activities in parallel and waits for all three with when_all

The unavailable branch calls the offerWaitlist activity, waits for the customer's decision with ctx.wait_for_external_event, ends as declined when the customer does not join the waitlist, and otherwise waits 2 days with ctx.create_timer and a 2-day timedelta before checking availability again

The workflow function contains no time.sleep, datetime.now or random calls, and the only TODO comments in the project are single `# TODO: implement actual functionality` markers inside activity bodies
The agent does not run `uv sync`, `pip install`, `dapr run` or `dapr init`

rentalBooking/README.md contains a mermaid diagram and `dapr run -f .` (or `dapr run -f dapr.yaml`), and the last output is exactly: The rentalBooking workflow application is created from the diagram. Open the README.md file in the rentalBooking folder for a summary and instructions for running locally. The extracted IR is stored at `rentalBooking/.workflow.ir.jsonl` for reference.

The returns back-edge (waitForReturns -> checkAvailability) is a bounded loop: no `while True`, a `MAX_..._ITERATIONS` constant limits the iterations, and the README records the limit and its exit path under "Open questions"
The agent writes .gitignore itself (no curl/wget/download of a .gitignore) and creates no virtual environment (no .venv folder, no uv.lock)

Dev Dashboard: before creating project files the agent runs `diagrid-dev-dashboard --version` once, does not ask about it, install it or stop because of it, and ends the final output with the matching Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation: if the command succeeded, how to start it (`diagrid-dev-dashboard`, http://localhost:9090); if it failed, how to install it (the install.sh and install.ps1 commands) — in both cases with a short reason it is useful and the link https://github.com/diagridio/dev-dashboard. No `--port 8080` and no container image is suggested

The generated README has a Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard section with the link https://github.com/diagridio/dev-dashboard, a short reason it is useful, the macOS / Linux install command (install.sh) and the Windows PowerShell install command (install.ps1), and how to run it (`diagrid-dev-dashboard`, http://localhost:9090); it does not mention a dashboard container image

evals.name: swimlane-image-to-csharp
evals.prompt: Turn this swimlane flowchart into a .NET (C#) Dapr workflow, project name UserOrder: skills/create-workflow-from-diagram/examples/user-order.png
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the image path, extracts participants, seven activities, two exclusive diverging gateways (with the change-request loop) and two end nodes into UserOrder/.workflow.ir.jsonl using the __type-keyed IR schema, then renders a C# project using Dapr.Workflow with a workflow class and one class per activity.
expectations: Creates UserOrder/.workflow.ir.jsonl whose first record has `__type: "metadata"` with `source: "image"`, and which contains `__type: "participant"` records for Customer, Sales Team, Inventory and Customer Service Department
The IR contains `__type: "activity"` records for Place Order, Check Order for Completeness, Request Changes, Update Order, Forward Order to Warehouse, Ship Items and Manage Refund

The IR contains two `__type: "gateway"` records with `type: "exclusive"` and `role: "diverging"` (Order complete? and Item in Stock?) whose `flows` carry Yes/No conditions with distinct `condition_label`s, and two `__type: "start_end_node"` records with `type: "end"` (Order Complete and Order Cancelled)
The IR contains an `__type: "edge"` record from Update Order back to Place Order, and ends with a `result` record with `success: true` followed by `end_of_ir_stream`

A .csproj in UserOrder references the Dapr.Workflow package, and a workflow class inherits Workflow<TInput, TOutput> while each activity is a separate class inheriting WorkflowActivity<TInput, TOutput>
The workflow class calls activities for Request Changes and Update Order on the incomplete-order branch and Manage Refund on the out-of-stock branch
The workflow class does not use DateTime.Now, DateTime.UtcNow, Guid.NewGuid() or new Random()

The last output is exactly: The UserOrder workflow application is created from the diagram. Open the README.md file in the UserOrder folder for a summary and instructions for running locally. The extracted IR is stored at `UserOrder/.workflow.ir.jsonl` for reference.

The generated C# project compiles: the grader runs `dotnet build` on the generated .csproj (on a copy or via a short path) and it succeeds with 0 errors; the agent itself does not run dotnet restore/build

The change-request loop re-runs the order-completeness check: after update_order (and place_order) the workflow calls check_order_completeness again, inside a loop whose condition is the order-complete decision (no `while (true)`), bounded by a MAX_..._ITERATIONS constant

evals.name: ambiguous-pizza-collaboration-to-javascript
evals.prompt: Generate a JavaScript Dapr workflow from skills/create-workflow-from-diagram/examples/pizza-order.png. Project name pizzaOrder.
evals.expected_output: pizza-order.png intentionally exercises the ambiguity/clarification path. The BPMN-style image has two pools linked by message flows, an event-based gateway racing a message against a 60-minute timer, and a disconnected branch (the 60-minute timer has no outgoing flow and 'call pizza delivery service' has no incoming flow). The skill models what is drawn in the __type-keyed IR, records the gap as a disconnected_flow unrecognized_item that needs the user's input, and in Phase 2 asks the user how the flows connect instead of inventing the edge or generating code.
expectations: Creates pizzaOrder/.workflow.ir.jsonl in which every record has a `__type` field, containing `__type: "participant"` records for the customer pool and the supplier side (pizza sale supplier or its lanes Pizza-Bäcker / Lieferjunge)

The IR contains a `__type: "gateway"` record with `type: "event-based"` after 'order pizza' whose `flows` have one entry with `event_type: "message"` (pizza received) and one with `event_type: "timer"` (60 minutes)
The dashed message flows between pools are not emitted as `edge` records; they are captured as message events, send or receive tasks, or `unrecognized_item` records with `category: "annotation"`

The missing connection between the 60-minute timer and 'call pizza delivery service' is recorded as an `unrecognized_item` with `category: "disconnected_flow"` and `ask_user: true`, the `metadata` record has `feedback_required: true`, and the IR contains no edge from the timer branch to 'call pizza delivery service'
The agent reports the disconnected flow to the user in plain language (no IR jargon) and asks how it should connect
The agent does not write workflow or activity code files in this run, because the open question is unresolved
The agent does not run `npm install` or `dapr run`
Because both pools contain their own process flow, the agent also asks which side to generate as the workflow (the customer pool, the supplier pool, or both) instead of silently picking one
